newsitem.title: UK: UK Referendum Party says will match Tory spending.
newsitem.headline: UK Referendum Party says will match Tory spending.

text.p: British millionaire Sir James Goldmsith said his Referendum Party would match or even top general election campaign spending by Britain's leading political parties.

Scotching a report in The Independent newspaper that his party was in crisis because it supporters were either too old or too thin on the ground, Goldsmith told BBC radio: "We will match the other parties or go higher and we're going to win more than one or two seats -- we are going to win a lot of seats."
Goldsmith's party wants to secure a referendum on whether Britain should adopt closer ties with the European Union.

Pressed on how much the party could afford to spend, Goldsmith said; "As high as we want. We will run a full campaign like any party...I certainly do not believe we shall be underspent by the Conservatives."
He said money was coming in from supporters and his family foundation would underwrite campaign expenses. The party had 2,000 prospective election candidates.

"We seek no power for ourselves whatsoever; only the power for people to decide for themselves on the single most important issue -- whether or not this nation should remain independent or whether it should be merged into an artificial European state."
